about.title: Care built around how patients actually age
body: GR ENT Diabetes & Geriatric Care Clinics was set up around a simple observation: ENT problems, diabetes, and the general health needs of older adults are rarely separate issues. Hearing loss, sinus trouble, blood sugar management, and age-related frailty often show up in the same patient, and in the same family.

Rather than sending patients across the city to three different specialists, we bring ENT care, diabetes management, and geriatric health support into a single clinic in Moulivakkam — with doctors who take the time to explain things clearly and never rush an elderly patient through a visit.

Whether you're bringing in a parent for a routine diabetes review, need a hearing assessment, or want a general health checkup for an older family member, our team is set up to handle it with patience and continuity of care.
highlights: Three specialities under one roof: ENT, diabetes, geriatric care

services.name: ENT Consultation & Treatment
services.tagline: Complete ear, nose, and throat care
services.overview: From routine ear infections to persistent sinus trouble, our ENT consultations cover diagnosis and treatment for the full range of ear, nose, and throat conditions affecting patients of all ages.
symptoms: Ear pain, discharge, or blocked sensation
Persistent nasal congestion or sinus pressure
Sore throat or hoarseness that won't resolve
Recurring throat infections
procedure: Detailed history and ENT examination
Diagnosis using clinical assessment and endoscopy where needed
Treatment plan — medication, minor procedure, or referral
Follow-up to confirm resolution
benefits: Same-day consultation for most ENT complaints
Clear explanation of diagnosis before treatment
Care coordinated with diabetes management when relevant
services.recovery: Most ENT conditions resolve within a few days to two weeks with appropriate treatment; minor in-clinic procedures typically need no downtime.

faqs.question: Do I need a referral to see the ENT specialist?
faqs.answer: No referral is needed — you can book an ENT consultation directly.

services.name: Hearing Assessment
services.tagline: Understanding hearing loss before it affects daily life
services.overview: Hearing loss is common among older adults and often goes unaddressed for years. Our hearing assessments identify the type and extent of hearing loss so we can recommend the right next step, whether that's treatment, monitoring, or a hearing aid referral.
symptoms: Difficulty following conversations, especially in groups
Frequently asking others to repeat themselves
Turning the TV or phone volume unusually high
Ringing or buzzing in the ears
procedure: Ear examination to rule out wax buildup or infection
Hearing evaluation appropriate to the patient's age and history
Discussion of results and practical next steps
Referral for hearing aids if required
benefits: No pressure to purchase devices you don't need
services.recovery: The assessment itself is non-invasive with no recovery time required.

services.name: Diabetes Management & Monitoring
services.overview: We help patients manage type 2 diabetes with regular monitoring, medication adjustment, and lifestyle guidance that's realistic for day-to-day life, not just a one-time prescription.
symptoms: Frequent thirst or urination
Unexplained fatigue
Slow-healing cuts or wounds
Blurred vision
procedure: Blood sugar review and history intake
Assessment of current medication and lifestyle factors
Personalized management plan with clear targets
Scheduled follow-up visits to track progress
benefits: Ongoing relationship with the same physician, not a new doctor each visit
Plans adjusted for elderly patients' overall health, not diabetes alone
Family involved in care planning where helpful
services.recovery: Diabetes management is ongoing rather than a one-time treatment; most patients settle into a stable routine within a few visits.

faqs.question: How often should I come in for diabetes review?
faqs.answer: Most patients are reviewed every 4–6 weeks initially, moving to longer intervals once blood sugar is well controlled.

services.name: Geriatric Health Checkups
services.tagline: Comprehensive health reviews for older adults
services.overview: Our geriatric checkups look at overall health in older patients — not just one complaint at a time — covering mobility, medication review, chronic conditions, and general wellbeing in a single unhurried visit.
symptoms: General decline in energy or mobility
Multiple ongoing medications needing review
Family concerns about a parent's overall health
No recent full health checkup
procedure: Extended consultation covering full medical history
Physical examination and basic diagnostics
Medication review to avoid unnecessary overlap
Written summary shared with patient and family
benefits: Unhurried appointment slots built specifically for elderly patients
Coordinated view across diabetes, ENT, and general health
Family members welcome to join the consultation
services.recovery: This is a consultative service with no recovery period involved.

faqs.question: Can a family member accompany an elderly patient during the checkup?
faqs.answer: Yes, we encourage it — having a family member present helps with both history-taking and understanding the follow-up plan.

services.name: Chronic Disease Management
services.overview: For patients managing diabetes alongside other chronic conditions such as hypertension or thyroid disorders, we provide coordinated, ongoing management rather than treating each condition in isolation.
symptoms: Multiple chronic conditions being managed separately
Difficulty keeping track of medications
Symptoms that seem connected across conditions
procedure: Review of all existing conditions and current treatment
Consolidated management plan across conditions
Regular monitoring visits
Adjustments based on progress
benefits: One doctor tracking the full picture, not fragmented care
Fewer, more useful visits instead of scattered appointments
Particularly suited to elderly patients with multiple conditions
services.recovery: Ongoing management rather than a fixed recovery timeline; review frequency is set based on condition stability.

services.overview: Not every visit needs a specialist. Our general health consultations cover common ailments, health concerns, and referrals for the whole family, alongside our ENT and diabetes-focused care.

General health concerns without a clear diagnosis
Need for a routine health checkup

Diagnosis and treatment, or referral to the appropriate specialist
Prescription and clear care instructions

Direct referral within the clinic when a speciality is needed

blogPosts.title: Why Hearing Loss and Diabetes Often Go Hand in Hand in Older Adults
blogPosts.excerpt: The two conditions show up together more often than most families realize — here's why, and what to watch for.
blogPosts.author: Dr. Ganesh Raman
content: It's a pattern we see often at the clinic: an elderly patient comes in for a diabetes review, and during the conversation it becomes clear they've also been struggling to follow conversations or have the television volume turned up unusually high.

Research has consistently found that people with diabetes are roughly twice as likely to experience hearing loss compared to those without it. High blood sugar levels over time can damage the small blood vessels and nerves in the inner ear, similar to the way diabetes affects the eyes and kidneys.

The tricky part is that hearing loss develops gradually, so patients and families often don't notice it until it starts affecting daily communication. That's why we recommend a simple hearing check as part of routine diabetes reviews for older patients, rather than waiting for a complaint.

The good news is that when caught early, hearing loss is very manageable, whether through monitoring, medical treatment, or a hearing aid referral. Combined with steady blood sugar control, most patients see a meaningful improvement in their day-to-day quality of life.

If you're managing diabetes for yourself or an elderly parent, it's worth asking your doctor for a hearing assessment alongside your regular diabetes checkup, especially if you've noticed conversations becoming harder to follow.
